study type: Simulation study using linked administrative data
cohort: All low-risk Australian women who gave birth, modeled using a population dataset from Queensland, Australia.
finding: Shifting low-risk births from hospitals to home birth or birth centers could result in significant hospital resource savings.
mod_finding: Hypothetically, if all low-risk women gave birth at home, cesarean rates would reduce from 13.4% to 2.7%, and if in birth centers, to 6.7%.
cross-section timing: Modelled for the year 2017, using administrative data from 2012-2015
